event_context: US delayed a planned tariff increase after progress in US-China trade talks; the CSI 300 rose 5.95%.
A renewed US tariff threat reversed trade-deal optimism and triggered a broad risk-off move.
Mainland markets reopened after an extended Lunar New Year break amid the initial COVID-19 outbreak; more than 3,000 shares hit limit-down.
Recovery hopes, policy support and state-media discussion of a healthy bull market accelerated a high-volume rally.
A domestic COVID surge, regulatory/delisting concerns and fear of possible China support for Russia pressured Chinese assets.
The State Council Financial Stability and Development Committee called for stable capital-market operation, prompting a sharp rebound.
Fears that Beijing could enter a Shanghai-style COVID lockdown intensified growth and supply-chain concerns.
Central Huijin expanded ETF purchases and regulators signalled stronger action to stabilize a market near five-year lows.
The PBOC announced rate and reserve-ratio cuts, property support and measures aimed at stabilizing stocks.
The late-September stimulus rally culminated in the strongest broad-market session in the sample.
Mainland markets reopened after the National Day holiday with pent-up demand, but gains narrowed after limited incremental fiscal detail.
The stimulus rally reversed sharply as investors took profits and reacted to disappointment over the scale and detail of follow-through.
China-US tariff retaliation deepened trade-war fears; the CSI 300 fell about 7% despite state-fund intervention.
Escalation in the US-Iran conflict raised oil, inflation and global-growth concerns, producing a broad Asia-Pacific risk-off session.
